evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.100: servus ille innocēns omnibus sententiīs absolvitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Each juror gave his sententia, so “unanimously” is omnibus sententiīs, “by all the votes”. Absolūtōrius is classical (Lewis & Short); condemnātōrius, Traupman’s word for a guilty verdict, is not found in Lewis & Short, where a jury simply condemnat.

phrases.english: to give a verdict of acquittal

phrases.source: Traupman 191, 197; Cic. Verr. 2.4.100 (Lewis & Short s.v. sententia)

sources: Lewis & Short: sententia · Lewis & Short: absolutorius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 197, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
